allowedPredicates: auth.uid()::text (actor self-derivation pins only, where a natural actor column exists)
forbiddenInPredicates: legacy domain helpers (the pre-J-005 domain tenancy/role reader pair)
domain role names (J-006: mapping lives in DomainDefinition.roleMappings)
policyConstructionLaw.holdsTenantRoleUsage: available but intentionally unused — no legitimate client path on these substrates requires a non-administrator role gate
policyConstructionLaw.provenanceLaw: no policy filters, mutates, or hides a provenance column; predicates reference only tenant_id and actor identity columns
policyConstructionLaw.multiTenantActor: SELECT raises AMBIGUOUS_TENANCY for multi-bound actors (fail-closed, observable); INSERT predicates are per-tenant via is_tenant_admin(row.tenant_id)

forceRls.safety: owner postgres holds the sanctioned BYPASSRLS attribute (verified live during the exemplar's authoring); SECURITY DEFINER primitives and gated RPCs unaffected; service_role holds the sanctioned platform bypass attribute — if absent, service_role sees zero rows (fail-closed)

privilegesConvention.authenticated: SELECT + INSERT only (no UPDATE/DELETE privilege — append-only substrates, least privilege)
privilegesConvention.anon: zero privileges, zero policy grants (untouched from source migrations)

tables.name: cg_reconciliation_input

absentPolicies.UPDATE: no policy and no privilege — append-only resolution law (Constitution §28)
absentPolicies.DELETE: no policy and no privilege — history preserved

tables.probeRationale: §4.4 data-declared recipe: the composite FK (verdict_row_id, tenant_id) requires a same-tenant privileged parent verdict row (probeAuxTables); the cross-tenant INSERT payload is fully constraint-valid so the denial is the is_tenant_admin WITH CHECK predicate, never a FK or CHECK error

tables.name: cg_reconciliation_verdict
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-035 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_reconciliation_verdict.md): verdicts are derived intelligence, never canonical truth a client consumes (Constitution §9), consumed only through the service-role-only reconciliation adapter that refuses policy-bearing clients; append-only integrity (§28) plus H2-04's recorded decision to grant the input sibling but deliberately exclude verdicts makes unchanged deny-by-default the confirmed V1 posture

tables.name: cg_event_security
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-035 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_event_security.md): per-event security contracts are inputs the consumption gate evaluates, not client surfaces (Constitution §35); digest-chain linkage and authority coordinates are minimization-class data with no declared V1 client purpose (§19), and the service-role-only event-security adapter is the single gate path — unchanged deny-by-default stands

tables.name: cg_event_security_denial
tables.clientWritePolicy: NONE — append-only gate denial audit (Constitution §28): no client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy is ever authored; rows are immutable gate decisions; reads remain service-role only
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-036 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_event_security_denial.md): every row is a gate DENY decision — audit, not content (Constitution §16); the append-only denial ledger must remain unwritable and unerazable by every client role (§28), delivery is gated before broadcast (§35), and no V1 client requirement exists — the deliberate absence of client policies is the security property, terminal for V1

tables.name: cg_event_security_redaction
tables.clientWritePolicy: NONE — append-only gate redaction audit (Constitution §28/§19): no client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy is ever authored; withheld-field records are immutable; reads remain service-role only
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-036 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_event_security_redaction.md): a redaction record discloses what was withheld and from whom — exposing it through any client policy would defeat the redaction itself (Constitution §19 minimization); the append-only withheld-fields ledger is the tamper-evidence that the original event was never silently altered (§28), REDACT outcomes are gate-owned audit rather than content (§16), and no V1 client path requires it

tables.name: cg_event_route_subscription

absentPolicies.UPDATE: no policy and no privilege — declaration immutability while it exists; a scope change is a retire plus a NEW subscription identity; suspension state transitions run server-side through the gated path
absentPolicies.DELETE: no policy and no privilege — unsubscribe is a state transition, never an erasure

tables.probeRationale: §4.4 data-declared recipe, no aux parent needed (no FK): the cross-tenant INSERT payload pins subscriber_id to the acting identity so the denial is the composite is_tenant_admin(TENANT_B)=false AND subscriber_id=auth.uid() WITH CHECK predicate, never a constraint error

tables.name: cg_event_route_queue
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-036 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_event_route_queue.md): the queue is routing-plane truth — which subscriber has what undelivered, in what order, under which gate decision — not a client surface (Constitution §35); deliveries are gated by the single enforcement point before enqueueing, so a client policy would create a second weaker gate over mutable delivery state, and subscribers observe delivery through their subscription outcomes, never the queue

tables.name: cg_event_route_cursor
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-037 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_event_route_cursor.md): the cursor is the router-owned one-way delivery frontier — no tenant actor holds a legitimate direct data-plane privilege in V1; zero policies is the strongest deny-by-default form (no policy expression anywhere can evaluate true), and any permissive policy would either expose tenant-sensitive frontier state or allow client-written rewind of delivery history (Constitution §35, §13)

tables.name: cg_event_route_outcome
tables.clientWritePolicy: NONE — append-only routing outcome audit (Constitution §28): no client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy is ever authored; every evaluation stays an unwritable, unerazable record; reads remain service-role only
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-037 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_event_route_outcome.md): an append-only routing outcome audit (Constitution §28) — every evaluation must remain an unwritable, unerazable record, so the absence of every client policy IS the security property; nothing silently dropped means nothing client-rewritable either, subscriber delivery is served by the gated queue/subscription surfaces, and forceRls=false is correct by posture law (FORCE cannot strengthen a no-policy posture)

tables.name: cg_evidence_record

policies.name: evidence_record_insert_tenant_admin
policies.predicate: public.is_tenant_admin(tenant_id) AND captured_by = auth.uid()::text AND created_by = auth.uid()::text

absentPolicies.UPDATE: no policy and no privilege — append-only lifecycle law: promotion/supersession/revocation are NEW records, the original is retained verbatim (E-018)
absentPolicies.DELETE: no policy and no privilege — revoked and superseded evidence is retained verbatim

tables.probeRationale: §4.4 data-declared recipe, no aux parent needed (self-referential FKs are nullable): the envelope is fully stamped (J-001/J-034 atomicity), canonical_truth_eligible satisfies the derived-flag CHECK, and the cross-tenant INSERT payload pins captured_by/created_by to the acting identity so the denial is the is_tenant_admin(TENANT_B)=false WITH CHECK predicate, never a constraint error

tables.name: cg_evidence_lifecycle_act
tables.clientWritePolicy: NONE — append-only lifecycle act ledger (Constitution §28): no client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy is ever authored; promotion/revocation/assessment acts are immutable records with actor and instant; reads remain service-role only
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-037 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_evidence_lifecycle_act.md): the act ledger is the tamper-evidence substrate of the evidence lifecycle (Constitution §28) — promotion/revocation/assessment acts are immutable records with a human, never AI, actor (§21), and a client policy would let a tenant actor forge validation history or erase a revocation; tenant-visible evidence is served by the policy-backed cg_evidence_record, and forceRls=false is correct by posture law

tables.name: cg_reasoning_provenance_snapshot
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-038 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_reasoning_provenance_snapshot.md): a snapshot is a data-provenance integrity surface (Constitution §12/§15) — generated_by_ai pinned true, verified pinned false — where client writability invites forged provenance and client readability widens an AI-provenance ledger before any authorization model for it exists; it is derived intelligence, never canonical truth (§9), and the service-role gateway path is the only consumer

tables.name: cg_usage_attribution_rollup
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-038 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_usage_attribution_rollup.md): roll-up headers are financial-metering aggregates consumed server-side (quota evaluation, metering) — no authorization model exists for who may read a tenant's money data (Constitution §16); token counts are observed reality while estimated cost is derived intelligence whose recorded integrity verdicts must not be rewritten or selectively read (§9, §28), and the H2-04 bucket/rollup split (bucket policy-backed, header zero-policy) is deliberate, not neglect

tables.name: cg_usage_attribution_bucket

absentPolicies.UPDATE: no policy and no privilege — the partition is immutable once persisted; defect reconciliation is a NEW roll-up
absentPolicies.DELETE: no policy and no privilege — the audit partition is never erased

tables.probeRationale: §4.4 data-declared recipe: the composite FK (rollup_row_id, tenant_id) requires a same-tenant privileged parent roll-up row (probeAuxTables); the cross-tenant INSERT payload is fully constraint-valid so the denial is the is_tenant_admin WITH CHECK predicate, never a FK or CHECK error

tables.name: cg_knowledge_source
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-038 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_knowledge_source.md): the source-reliability registry is epistemic governance, not client content — a client-writable policy would let callers mint or move trust tiers, and every downstream knowledge record inherits its source's current tier at query time (Constitution §9/§11/§12); same-tenant acts are already composite-FK-enforced (§17/§28), so zero-policy deny for all client roles is strictly stronger than any tenant-scoped predicate for a table with no legitimate client consumer

tables.name: cg_knowledge_freshness_contract
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-039 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_knowledge_freshness_contract.md): the freshness contract is the platform-side declaration of when a memory record's currency (fresh/stale) may be asserted — part of the §9 canonical-truth validation substrate, enforced server-side by the pure contract plus the service-role adapter; no V1 API or page consumes the rows, the database itself refuses all client access (§17/§34), and composite FKs make cross-tenant contracts unbindable

tables.name: cg_knowledge_invalidation
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-039 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_knowledge_invalidation.md): the tombstone act ledger removes a knowledge record from current without deleting it (ADR-005, Constitution §9) — if it were client-mutable or client-erasable, stale knowledge could be resurrected or valid knowledge silently killed; substrate-unique one-act-per-record plus the evidence requirement plus zero client privilege make it tamper-evident by posture (§28), and no V1 client surface exists

tables.name: cg_knowledge_downgrade
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-039 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_knowledge_downgrade.md): the downgrade act ledger records who demoted a source's reliability tier, why, and with what evidence — the enforcement record behind trust-never-rises-silently (G-047/G-052); strict-down CHECK, evidence requirement and same-tenant composite FK carry the semantics in the database (Constitution §28), while zero-policy plus privilege revocation ensure no client can write, mutate, or erase a demotion or launder untrusted output provenance (§9/§21)

tables.name: cg_tool_runtime_tool
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-040 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_tool_runtime_tool.md): the only access path is the service-role tool-runtime adapter (client privileges fully revoked), so a client policy would be dead code or would require widening grants first (Constitution §16/§17); AI-proposal gating (capability gate, credential-lease mediation, delegation bounding) happens upstream of the data plane (§21), and the tenant_id parameterization is unresolved (COND-003) — authoring a tenant-scoped policy on an unstable type risks the exact widening the posture forbids

tables.name: cg_tool_runtime_invocation
tables.rationale: adjudicated zero-policy-by-design by H3-040 (architecture/campaigns/h3/posture-adjudication/cg_tool_runtime_invocation.md): invocations are the audited output of the Constitution §21 AI-proposal chain — capability gate, delegation bounding, credential-lease mediation — not a client surface; the append-only ledger must stay unwritable and unerazable by any client path (§28), client reads would expose tenant-wide tool-invocation history without purpose/policy context (§19), and COND-003 leaves the tenant_id parameterization unresolved

tables.name: cg_file_object

absentPolicies.DELETE: no policy and no privilege — removal is a tombstone transition via deleted_at (Constitution §28)

tables.probeRationale: §4.4 data-declared recipe: the cross-tenant INSERT payload is fully constraint-valid (content_ref template-resolves to the TENANT_B-prefixed path, satisfying the derived CHECK) so the denial is the file_object_insert_own_tenant WITH CHECK predicate (tenant-equality AND owner self-derivation), never a CHECK or FK error. The $template value form exists because the content_ref CHECK derives from the row tenant — inexpressible with exact-match placeholders.

tables.name: cg_idempotency_record

policies.name: idempotency_record_replace_expired
policies.predicate: USING: tenant_id = public.get_my_tenant_id() AND expires_at <= now(); WITH CHECK: tenant_id = public.get_my_tenant_id() AND public.is_tenant_admin(tenant_id) AND actor_id = auth.uid()::text

absentPolicies.DELETE: no policy and no privilege for any client role — the only deletion surface is the service-role-only SECURITY DEFINER prune of expired rows (exactly-once substrate cannot be sabotaged through the client boundary)

tables.probeRationale: §4.4 data-declared recipe: the id column is omitted (uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()), all CHECK constraints are satisfied with static values (64-hex digests, expires_at > created_at, bounded lengths), so the cross-tenant INSERT denial is the idempotency_record_insert_tenant_admin WITH CHECK predicate (is_tenant_admin on TENANT_B is false for the tenant-A-bound actor) — never a constraint error. UPDATE is replace-expired-only and there is NO client DELETE.

batteryExpectations.crossTenantProbeLaw: for each policy-backed table: an authenticated actor bound to tenant A must see zero rows of tenant B for all four commands; an unbound actor must see zero rows; AMBIGUOUS_TENANCY must raise; anon must be denied by privilege; insert probes must fail the is_tenant_admin predicate for non-administrators and the auth.uid() self-derivation pins where present
batteryExpectations.genuineInverse: the rollback must restore relforcerowsecurity=false, zero policies, and the source-migration grant state (anon/authenticated revoked, service_role silent) on exactly the six policy-backed tables — and nothing else
